DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

The clinical picture of a non-smoking 51-year-old with an 11-year history of chronic cough, copious purulent sputum, and recurrent "bronchitis" is highly characteristic of bronchiectasis. While alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency is a consideration given the chronicity, the severity and nature of your sputum strongly point to structural airway damage. Have you noticed any hemoptysis or shortness of breath, and do you have a family history of lung or liver disease?
